concerns.text: FR-002/FR-004 retrieve WorldClim 'monthly temperature, precipitation' for each sample's 'sampling date'. WorldClim provides long-term climatological normals (19 bioclim variables), NOT date-specific observed weather. Aligning a sample's sampling date to WorldClim is a category error: the predictor is the same for all samples at a location regardless of year/season. Either use an actual historical weather product (e.g. ERA5/CHIRPS) or drop the date-matching claim; as written the 'temporal alignment' (Constitution VI) is illusory.

The design stratifies by stress type (drought/salinity/metal toxicity) but stress type is not listed as a predictor, and species, organ/tissue, developmental stage, and study-of-origin are not controlled anywhere. In public metabolomics repositories, metabolite variance is dominated by species and batch/study effects; without including or adjusting for these, any environment→metabolite R² is confounded and uninterpretable. The spec must specify how species/study confounding is handled (e.g. include as covariates, or within-species analysis).

FR-010/SC-002 apply a 'two-sided test' for whether permutation importance differs from zero. Permutation importance (decrease in R² on shuffling) is non-negative by construction, so a two-sided test is ill-posed; and the 95% bootstrap CI already contains the zero-comparison. Specify a one-sided test or rely on the bootstrap CI excluding zero.

FR-008/SC-003 report metrics per metabolite but not per stress category, while Constitution Principle VII mandates per-stress-type reporting before any aggregate metric. Pooling R² across drought/salinity/metal-toxicity samples conflates distinct biological regimes and can mask that environmental drivers explain variance in only one stratum. Add per-stress reporting to FR-008.

Random train/validation/test split (FR-006) on samples drawn from few public studies risks leakage: samples from the same study/species/site appearing in both train and test, inflating out-of-sample R². Specify grouping (e.g. GroupKFold by study or species) for the split.
